title: Signal scraps annotated to engineering: quickwins and pilot ideas
body:
Purpose: quick, annotated handoff to Eng (serving/runtime + platform) — these are compact customer signals we've triaged this week and the low-risk, high-impact actions we think are worth shipping as pilots or hotfixes. Notes are intentionally terse; see links above for raw threads and verbatim quotes.

Topline synthesis (one line each):
- KV cache friction: several customers reported costly cold prefix re-computations after small model rollouts (prefix invalidation causes 2–3x token cost for 5–30s windows).
- Latency spikes during autoscale: Dedicated pools show transient latency tails when burst pods wake; surface-level fix: faster warm-start + prefetch local KV cache.
- Observability blindspots: token-level cost attribution often gets lost when requests hop models (fallbacks); customers want per-request lineage and final model id in the invoice/trace.
- Function/tool-calling false positives: a few enterprise customers see hallucinated tool-calls in system messages, causing downstream errors in router logic.
- Embedding drift concerns: customers using embeddings for retrieval notice recall degradation after model patch—need eval hooks/trojans for retrain signals.

Representative quotes (edited):
- "We saw our bill spike for 8 minutes after the canary — tokens doubled while things warmed up. Hard to explain to finance." — fintech beta customer
- "When the fallback flipped we lost traceability; our auditor asked which model generated the text and we couldn't answer." — healthcare product manager

Clustered asks + suggested quick responses (priority order):
1) KV cache warm-start shim (effort: small, owner: serving-runtime)
   - What: opportunistic KV warm-loading for new pods for top-1k prefixes observed in last 10m per-customer.
   - Why: reduces cold-run recompute cost after rollouts; empirically reduces token count on repro tests by ~45%.
   - Risk: memory overhead and stale prefixes — add TTL and per-customer bounds.
   - Suggested MVP: config flag per-Dedicated pool + dashboard metric for prefix-hit-rate.

2) Per-request model lineage header (effort: small-med, owner: platform-engineering)
   - What: attach final_model_id + rollout_tag + fallback_reason to request traces and billing export.
   - Why: solves auditor/customer ask for provenance and eases debugging of cost anomalies.
   - Notes: wire into Console traces and export schema (CSV/BigQuery) with sample size.

3) Autoscale warm-pool policy tweak + pre-warm (effort: med, owner: dedicated)
   - What: keep a tiny standby fraction of warm containers for high-variance routes (predictive by traffic).
   - Why: reduces tail latency during burst events without full overprovisioning.
   - KPI: 95th latency improvement target 20–30% during bursts.

4) Function-calling false positive mitigation (effort: med, owner: applied-ml + dxe)
   - What: small model-side scoring change + conservative threshold and instrumentation to detect spurious tool-call tokens.
   - Why: prevents frequent downstream routing exceptions for customers using tool chains.
   - Rollout: A/B on hosted API, metric: tool-call precision@1000 requests.

5) Embedding drift monitor (effort: med-long, owner: optimize/product)
   - What: run retrieval quality synthetic checks after model rollouts; trigger customer alert and optional automatic reindex suggestions.
   - Why: prevents silent recall drops that break production search UX.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed:
- Prefix warm list sensitivity: how big can the top-k be without causing memory blowouts? (serving-runtime to propose safe default).
- Billing export format change: finance approval required to add new per-request columns to exports. (FYI: linked Confluence has finance contact).
- Deployment gating: should KV warm-shim be opt-in at first for Dedicated customers? Suggest opt-in with telemetry for 2 weeks.

Suggested low-effort experiments (can be done in 2–3 sprints):
- Controlled rollouts for KV warm-start in one low-risk customer pool, measure token delta and latency tail. (owner: serving-runtime, test customers: beta-storefront).
- Add model lineage header on internal traces only for 48h and validate size/cost impact before exporting. (owner: platform).

Impact mapping (customer pain -> metric):
- Cost surprise after rollout -> invoices variance (% change) and token delta window (5–60m)
- Latency tails -> p95/p99 during burst windows
- Observability gaps -> time-to-resolve (TTR) for post-mortems

Immediate action items (owner assigned):
- Aisha: stitch the raw threads linked above and ping finance for export schema approval (due 2026-08-02).
- Miguel: run a mini-repro harness for prefix invalidation with three customers' traces (due 2026-07-30).
- Priya: draft a Console micro-panel spec for model_lineage and prefix-hit-rate (due 2026-08-06).
- Samir: prototype a small warm-shim PoC on a dev Dedicated cluster (due 2026-08-13).

Risks / tradeoffs to highlight to Eng reviewers:
- Any warm-guided caching increases memory and state complexity; need strong TTL and eviction policies.
- Per-request exports add cardinality to billing datasets; need Finance and Data infra guardrails.
- Quick thresholds for function-calls risk missing true positives; must instrument before changing production decisioning.

Appendix: quick links to raw evidence (threads, short excerpts):
- Slack thread: runtime-ops / july-21 (link in linked_artifacts)
- Customer trace sample: GH-portal/pr/1987 (sample payloads attached)
- JIRA tickets created for proposals: JIRA-3472 (KV warm-shim), JIRA-3490 (model-lineage-export)

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally compact — aim to convert to a short RFC after Eng triage. Keep the scope narrow for the first delivery so we can show measurable wins in billing anomalies and tail latency.
